senses.gloss: (v. סוּם II) to tie up, close; to make blind.—Part. pass. סָמוּי; f. סְמוּיָה, סְמוּיָיה; pl. סְמוּיִים, סְמוּיִין; סְמוּיוֹת

units: <cite ref="Taanit 8b:13">Taan. 8ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <he>אסמיך</he>, <cite ref="Deuteronomy 28:8">Deut. XXVIII, 8</cite>) <he>דבר הס׳ מן העין</he> that which is hidden from sight (the exact quantity of which you do not know); <cite ref="Bava Metzia 42a">B. Mets. 42ᵃ</cite>; a. e.—
senses.label: a

units: <cite ref="Kiddushin 24b:12">Kidd. 24ᵇ</cite> <he>הרי שהיתה עינו ס׳ וכ׳</he> if the slave’s eye was blind, and he (the master) cut it out.
<cite ref="Ketubot 105a:15">Keth. 105ᵃ</cite> <he>כמה ס׳ עיניהם וכ׳</he> how blind are the eyes of (how short-sighted are) those who receive bribes!
senses.label: b

senses.gloss: to blind, make blind. Kidd. l. c. סי׳ עובר וכ׳ he injured the eye of the embryo (while operating on the mother). Ib. הרי שהיתה … וסִמְּאָהּ suppose the slave’s eye was dim, and he (the master) made it entirely blind. Y. Kil. VIII, 31ᶜ top וסִימְּיָיהּ; B. Kam. 91ᵃ וסִימְּאוֹ (Ms. M. וסימאה) and he made him blind.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 8:7">Ib. VIII, 7</cite> <he>האומר סַמֵּא וכ׳</he> if one says (to his neighbor), blind my eye, the neighbor is responsible.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 75">Gen. R. s. 75</cite>, end <he>לו … לסַמּוֹת וכ׳ שלח</he> he sent him a present in order to blind his eyes (with ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 16:19">Deut. XVI, 19</cite>).
<cite ref="Shabbat 109a:1">Sabb. 109ᵃ</cite> top <he>יד מְסַמְּאָה</he> an unwashed hand put on the eye makes blind.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 42">Gen. R. s. 42</cite> (ref. to <he>עין משפט</he>, <cite ref="Genesis 14:7">Gen. XIV, 7</cite> <he>עין … לסַמּוֹתָהּ</he> they wanted to blind the eye (of him) that established the rule of justice in the world; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to tie up one’s own eyes; to simulate blindness.
units: <cite ref="Tosefta Peah 4:14">Tosef. Peah IV, 14</cite>; Y. ib. VIII, 21ᵇ top; <cite ref="Ketubot 68a:3">Keth. 68ᵃ</cite> <he>המְסמֵּא את עינו</he> (a beggar) who ties his eye up.

<cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 5:5">Bekh. V, 5</cite> (<cite ref="Bekhorot 36b:16">36ᵇ</cite>) <he>שנִסְמֵת עינו</he> (Talm. ed. <he>שנִסְמֵית</he>) that became blind on one eye; <cite ref="Ketubot 77a:5">Keth. 77ᵃ</cite> <he>נִיסְמֵת</he>; a. fr.
<cite ref="Arakhin 17b">Arakh. 17ᵇ</cite>, sq. <he>פִּתֵּחַ ונ׳</he> if he was open-eyed and became blind; <cite ref="Bava Batra 128a">B. Bath. 128ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 18:22">Num. R. s. 18</cite> <he>מיד היה מִסְתַּמֵּא</he> (not <he>היתה</he>) he would get blind at once; a. e.
